subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should local avatar failures keep the current generic direct-route 404 with clearer authenticated UI metadata diagnostics, or should `/avatar/{agentId}` expose specific statuses/messages for oversized, missing, or rejected files?
rationale: The choice affects an authenticated local workspace file-serving path: more specific direct-route errors improve UX but may disclose local policy or file-state details, while UI-only diagnostics preserve the existing direct image route boundary.

options.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using metadata reasons and Control UI surfaces to show clear oversized, missing-file, unsupported-type, or outside-workspace guidance.

options.title: Expose Endpoint Errors
options.body: Return specific 4xx statuses such as 413 or 400 from the avatar endpoint, with security review and tests proving no unsafe path details leak.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Avatar Contract
options.body: Defer the local diagnostics decision into the broader remote/local avatar policy work tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41201.

recommendation.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using metadata reasons and Control UI surfaces to show clear oversized, missing-file, unsupported-type, or outside-workspace guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for both the original avatar route and the later security hardening that any diagnostics change must preserve.
